stories.headline: Anthropic Hits $1 Trillion Valuation on Secondary Markets, Surpassing OpenAI's $880B on Forge Global

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's valuation on Forge Global, a leading private marketplace exchange, has hit approximately $1 trillion, surpassing OpenAI which trades at $880 billion on the same platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Desperate buyers are in a race to secure a dwindling supply of secondary shares in Anthropic. One shareholder recently offered to sell shares at a $1.15 trillion valuation.

key_facts.fact: On Hiive, another secondary marketplace, Anthropic share prices surged 211% to roughly $900 over the past three months, while OpenAI shares rose only 8.5% to $608 in the same period.
key_facts.excerpt: Private stock market Hiive informed The Post that the price for Anthropic shares has surged 211% to roughly $900 over the previous three months. Shares of OpenAI have risen just 8.5% to $608 over the same period.

key_facts.fact: The surge is driven by Anthropic's rapid revenue growth — from $9 billion at end of 2025 to over $30 billion by end of March 2026 — and strong adoption of Claude Code.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has also seen enormous income growth, from $9 billion at the finish of 2025 to over $30 billion by the finish of March. The company credited widespread adoption of its commercially accessible Claude services for the surge.

key_facts.fact: Glen Anderson, CEO of Rainmaker Securities, said he received an offer to buy Anthropic shares at a $960 billion valuation — 'an unthinkable price even just weeks ago.' A separate offer from a 'very well-known growth fund' came in at $1.05 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: 'It's been an epic run for Anthropic,' Glen Anderson, CEO of Rainmaker Securities, said. 'Everybody desires to be half of a generational alternative in AI, and proper now, Anthropic is in the pole place.'

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's last primary funding round valued the company at $380 billion; the secondary market premium implies ~2.6x that valuation. OpenAI's last primary round was $852 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has a $1 trillion secondary market valuation compared to a $380 billion actual valuation, possibly signaling more room for growth. Meanwhile, OpenAI's secondary valuation of $880 billion is just $30 billion less than the actual $850 billion valuation.

stories.headline: Anthropic Publishes Postmortem on Claude Code Quality Drop: Three Bugs Fixed, Usage Limits Reset

key_facts.fact: Anthropic traced Claude Code quality complaints to three separate changes: reduced default reasoning effort (March 4), a caching bug that cleared thinking every turn (March 26), and a system prompt limiting responses to ≤25 words between tool calls (April 16).
key_facts.excerpt: We've traced these reports to three separate changes that affected Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, and Claude Cowork. The API was not impacted.

key_facts.fact: The reasoning effort change reduced default from 'high' to 'medium' to cut latency; Anthropic called it 'the wrong tradeoff' and reverted on April 7. All users now default to 'xhigh' for Opus 4.7 and 'high' for other models.
key_facts.excerpt: We changed Claude Code's default reasoning effort from 'high' to 'medium' to reduce the very long latency. This was the wrong tradeoff. We reverted this change on April 7.

key_facts.fact: The caching bug was meant to clear old thinking from idle sessions once, but instead cleared it every turn, making Claude 'forgetful and repetitive.' It passed multiple layers of review before being caught.
key_facts.excerpt: A bug caused this to keep happening every turn for the rest of the session instead of just once, which made Claude seem forgetful and repetitive.

key_facts.fact: The verbosity-reduction system prompt caused a measurable 3% drop in coding benchmarks for both Opus 4.6 and 4.7, and was reverted on April 20. All issues resolved in v2.1.116.
key_facts.excerpt: One of these evaluations showed a 3% drop for both Opus 4.6 and 4.7. We immediately reverted the prompt as part of the April 20 release.

key_facts.fact: As compensation, Anthropic reset usage limits for all subscribers. The company also set up the @ClaudeDevs X account for more transparent communication of product decisions.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropics also set up the X account @ClaudeDevs to communicate product decisions more transparently.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is adding tighter controls: broader per-model eval suites for every system prompt change, soak periods, gradual rollouts, and new tooling to make prompt changes easier to review and audit.
key_facts.excerpt: We're also adding tighter controls on system prompt changes. We will run a broad suite of per-model evals for every system prompt change to Claude Code.

stories.headline: Cohere Acquires Germany's Aleph Alpha in $20B Sovereign AI Deal, Schwarz Group Invests $600M

key_facts.fact: Canadian AI startup Cohere agreed to acquire German AI startup Aleph Alpha in a deal valuing the combined entity at approximately $20 billion. Cohere shareholders receive ~90% of the combined company, Aleph Alpha's ~10%.
key_facts.excerpt: Cohere's shareholders will receive approximately 90% of the combined entity, while Aleph's shareholders are expected to receive approximately 10%. The combined valuation of $20 billion reflects a significant premium over both companies' last known marks.

key_facts.fact: Schwarz Group, which owns retailers Lidl and Kaufland, will invest $600 million in Cohere's upcoming Series E round as part of the deal. Cohere was last valued at $6.8 billion in August 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Schwarz Group — a key backer of Aleph Alpha — plans to invest $600 million in Cohere's upcoming Series E round. Cohere last raised $500 million in fresh capital in August 2025, bringing its valuation to $6.8 billion.

key_facts.fact: Global HQ stays in Toronto, European HQ in Berlin. Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez remains CEO. Germany's Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger and Canada's AI Minister Evan Solomon attended the Berlin announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: The combined entity will have its global headquarters in Toronto and its European headquarters in Berlin. The deal is supported by the Canadian and German governments.

key_facts.fact: The deal targets sovereign AI for regulated sectors — public sector, finance, defense, energy, healthcare — giving Cohere access to Aleph Alpha's existing German government contracts including the ministry for digital affairs.
key_facts.excerpt: Cohere will look to boost its offering of secure customized AI for highly-regulated sectors. Aleph Alpha's existing commercial contracts with the German public sector were also an attraction.

key_facts.fact: Cohere CFO Francois Chadwick told Reuters: 'We are going to commit to working with European infrastructure and maintain the sovereignty requirements that are being addressed in Europe.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We are bringing Aleph Alpha into Cohere, and we are going to merge the two entities,' Cohere CFO Francois Chadwick told Reuters. 'We are going to commit to working with European infrastructure … and maintain the sovereignty requirements.'

stories.headline: Cursor Hit $2.7B Annualized Revenue in March, Up 14x YoY, as Gross Margins Turn Positive

stories.headline: DeepSeek Releases V4-Pro (1.6T Params) and V4-Flash, Largest Open-Source Models With 1M Context

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 1.6T total parameters with 49B active (MoE), pre-trained on 33T tokens. V4-Flash has 284B total with 13B active, trained on 32T tokens. Both support 1M token context.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 1.6T total / 49B active params. Performance rivaling the world's top closed-source models. DeepSeek-V4-Flash: 284B total / 13B active params. Your fast, efficient, and economical choice.

key_facts.fact: V4-Pro is the largest open-weights model released, bigger than Kimi K2.6 (1.1T) and GLM-5.1 (754B), and more than twice the size of DeepSeek V3.2 (685B).
key_facts.excerpt: I think this makes DeepSeek-V4-Pro the new largest open weights model. It's larger than Kimi K2.6 (1.1T) and GLM-5.1 (754B) and more than twice the size of DeepSeek V3.2 (685B).

key_facts.fact: V4-Pro API pricing is $1.74/1M input tokens and $3.48/1M output; V4-Flash is $0.14/1M input and $0.28/1M output — the cheapest in both model tiers.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek-V4-Flash is the cheapest of the small models, beating even OpenAI's GPT-5.4 Nano. DeepSeek-V4-Pro is the cheapest of the larger frontier models.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek says V4-Pro trails state-of-the-art frontier models (GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1-Pro) by approximately 3 to 6 months, and is the strongest open-source model in coding and math benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Against the current closed-source frontier, OpenAI's GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1-Pro — the company says V4-Pro falls only 'marginally short,' and offers a candid self-assessment: its 'developmental trajectory' trails state-of-the-art frontier models by approximately 3 to 6 months.

key_facts.fact: V4 introduces a hybrid attention mechanism (Compressed Sparse Attention + Heavily Compressed Attention) that reduces KV cache to 10% and single-token FLOPs to 27% of V3.2 at 1M context.
key_facts.excerpt: In the scenario of 1M-token context, even DeepSeek-V4-Pro attains only 27% of the single-token FLOPs and 10% of the KV cache size relative to DeepSeek-V3.2.

key_facts.fact: Both models are open-sourced under the MIT license on Hugging Face. The release was timed to coincide with OpenAI's GPT-5.5 launch on the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: This repository and the model weights are licensed under the MIT License.

key_facts.fact: Huawei announced its Ascend supernode based on the Ascend 950 AI chips will fully support DeepSeek V4. DeepSeek says V4-Pro throughput is currently limited by high-end compute supply, with prices expected to drop when Huawei Ascend 950 super nodes ship at scale in H2.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek worked with Chinese AI chipmakers Huawei and Cambricon to optimise V4 for their latest hardware. The company did not give Nvidia or AMD early access for optimisation.

stories.headline: EU Approves €90B Loan for Ukraine and 20th Sanctions Package After Hungary Lifts Veto

key_facts.fact: The EU approved a €90 billion ($106 billion) loan package for Ukraine to cover economic and military needs for the next two years, after Hungary lifted its veto.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine desperately needs the 90-billion-euro ($106 billion) loan package to prop up its war-ravaged economy and help keep Russian forces at bay. Hungary angered its EU partners by reneging on a December deal to provide the funds.

key_facts.fact: Russian oil resumed flowing through the Druzhba pipeline to Slovakia after a three-month halt, removing the key obstacle to Hungary and Slovakia lifting their veto.
key_facts.excerpt: The flow resumed after three months at 2 a.m. Thursday, the Slovak economy ministry said, lifting a major obstacle to approving the EU funds for Ukraine later Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The 20th sanctions package targets Russian energy revenues, shadow fleet, crypto, and military-industrial complex, banning transactions with 20 Russian banks and imposing a sectoral ban on Russian crypto providers.
key_facts.excerpt: Transaction ban on 20 Russian banks. Sectoral ban on Russian crypto providers/platforms. Ban on transactions in RUBx (Russian crypto) and EU operators access for the digital rouble.

key_facts.fact: 46 additional vessels were banned (total: 632), and the EU activated its anti-circumvention tool for the first time, restricting exports to Kyrgyzstan over re-exports of sanctioned goods to Russia.
key_facts.excerpt: 46 additional vessels banned (total: 632), targeting shadow fleet tankers. Ban for EU operators to export CNC machines and certain radios to Kyrgyzstan (high re-export risk to Russia).

key_facts.fact: The sanctions include expanded export bans worth €360M+ and import bans worth €570M+, covering lab glassware, lubricants, chemicals, metals, and minerals.
key_facts.excerpt: Expanded export bans (€360M+ value): Laboratory glassware, high-performance lubricants, energetic materials, chemicals. Expanded import bans (€570M+ value): Raw materials, metals, minerals, steel scraps.

key_facts.fact: 16 entities in third countries (China, UAE, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Belarus) face sanctions for supplying dual-use goods or weapons to Russia.
key_facts.excerpt: Including 16 entities in third countries (China, UAE, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Belarus) supplying dual-use goods/weapons to Russia.

stories.headline: FDA Approves Regeneron's Otarmeni, First Gene Therapy for Genetic Hearing Loss, Free in the US

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval for Otarmeni (lunsotogene parvec-cwha), the first gene therapy for genetic hearing loss and the first FDA-approved gene therapy to restore a neurosensory function to normal levels.
key_facts.excerpt: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. has received accelerated approval for OtarmeniTM, the first gene therapy and second new molecular entity approved under the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher program.

key_facts.fact: In the CHORD trial, 80% of the 20 evaluable pediatric patients achieved or surpassed the primary hearing endpoint at week 24, and with longer follow-up, 42% achieved normal hearing.
key_facts.excerpt: Pivotal results of the CHORD trial demonstrating 80% of participants achieved or surpassed a hearing level meeting the primary endpoint, and with longer follow-up, 42% achieved normal hearing.

key_facts.fact: Regeneron will make Otarmeni available for free in the United States and announced a drug pricing deal with the White House.
key_facts.excerpt: Regeneron said the therapy Otarmeni will be available for free to patients in the United States. Regeneron is also set to announce a drug pricing deal with the White House this afternoon.

key_facts.fact: OTOF-related hearing loss is ultra-rare, affecting 20-50 newborns per year in the US. Otarmeni delivers a functioning OTOF gene to inner ear hair cells via an infusion into the cochlea under general anesthesia.
key_facts.excerpt: OTOF hearing loss is ultra-rare, diagnosed in about 50 newborns per year in the U.S., according to Regeneron.

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Otarmeni just 61 days after Regeneron submitted its biologics license application, making it the sixth approval under the National Priority Voucher program and the first for a gene therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA said it approved Otarmeni 61 days after Regeneron submitted its biologics license application. It's the sixth approval under this program and the first for a gene therapy.

key_facts.fact: Regeneron acquired Decibel Therapeutics, which originally developed the therapy (then called DB-OTO), in 2023 for up to $213 million including milestones.

stories.headline: TerraPower Begins Construction on First Next-Gen Nuclear Plant in the US, a 345MW Natrium Reactor

key_facts.fact: TerraPower officially started construction on Kemmerer Unit 1 in Wyoming on April 23, the first utility-scale advanced nuclear power plant in the United States
key_facts.excerpt: TerraPower, a nuclear innovation company, today, announced the official start of construction on its flagship Natrium® plant, Kemmerer Unit 1. Kemmerer Unit 1 is on track to be the first utility-scale advanced nuclear power plant in the United States.

key_facts.fact: The NRC construction permit issued in March 2026 was the first for a commercial non-light water reactor in more than 40 years and the first for any commercial reactor in nearly a decade
key_facts.excerpt: The construction start follows the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission's (NRC's) issuance of a construction permit on March 4, 2026—the first the agency has granted for a commercial non–light water reactor in more than 40 years and the first for any commercial reactor in nearly a decade.

key_facts.fact: The Natrium plant features a 345MW sodium-cooled fast reactor with molten salt thermal storage that can boost output to 500MW for over 5 hours during peak demand
key_facts.excerpt: The facility includes a 345-megawatt, sodium-cooled fast reactor equipped with a system that captures excess heat within the molten salt. Tapping a thermal salt battery can boost the plant's power to 500 megawatts for more than five hours.

key_facts.fact: The project is backed by up to $2 billion in cost-shared federal support through DOE's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program; founded by Bill Gates
key_facts.excerpt: Founded by Bill Gates and backed by up to $2 billion in cost-shared federal support through DOE's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program (ARDP).

key_facts.fact: TerraPower aims for nuclear fission reactor operational by end of 2030; about 1,600 workers during construction and 250 permanent once operational
key_facts.excerpt: At peak construction, the project is expected to employ around 1,600 workers. Once operational, it is projected to support approximately 250 permanent jobs at the facility.

stories.headline: Trump Threatens 'Big Tariff' on UK If It Doesn't Drop Its 2% Digital Services Tax

key_facts.fact: Trump told reporters at the White House that the US will 'put a big tariff on the UK' if Britain does not drop its digital services tax, which he views as unfairly targeting American tech companies like Apple, Google, and Meta.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump said the United States will retaliate with a 'big tariff' if Britain continues to target companies like Apple, Alphabet's Google and Meta with its technology tax.

key_facts.fact: The UK's 2% digital services tax, introduced in 2020, generated £944 million in the 2025-26 fiscal year (up 17% YoY) and is projected to raise £1.4 billion annually by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Recent data from HM Revenue and Customs showed that the DST generated £944 million in the 2025–26 fiscal year, up 17% from the previous year. Official projections suggest the tax could raise £1.4 billion annually by 2030.

key_facts.fact: The warning comes ahead of King Charles III's state visit to the US next week; Trump said the monarch could help repair Washington's relationship with Britain, which has become strained.
key_facts.excerpt: His comments come ahead of a visit by Britain's head of state, King Charles, next week. Trump said he believes the monarch could help repair the Washington's relationship with the British.

key_facts.fact: Trump said: 'I don't like it when they target American companies, because basically, you're talking about our great American companies... We've been looking at it, and we can meet that very easily by just putting a big tariff on the UK.'

key_facts.fact: The DST has been criticized by both Trump and his predecessor Joe Biden. The UK has so far resisted Washington's calls to drop the tax, maintaining it ensures digital businesses contribute fairly based on their economic activity in the country.

stories.headline: US Accuses China of Industrial-Scale AI Distillation; Beijing Orders Tech Firms to Reject US Capital

key_facts.fact: White House OSTP Director Michael Kratsios wrote in a memo that the US has intelligence indicating 'foreign entities, principally based in China' are conducting 'industrial-scale distillation' of American AI models using tens of thousands of surrogate accounts.
key_facts.excerpt: Foreign entities primarily based in China have conducted 'industrial-scale' campaigns to crib frontier AI models from US companies, Michael Kratsios, White House director of the office of science and technology policy, said in a memo.

key_facts.fact: The White House plans to share intelligence with US AI companies, coordinate private-sector defenses, develop best practices, and explore measures to hold foreign actors accountable for distillation campaigns.
key_facts.excerpt: The administration said it would work with US AI firms to counter such campaigns; the companies themselves recently banded together to share information about so-called adversarial distillation attempts.

key_facts.fact: In a parallel move, Chinese regulators including the NDRC told tech firms such as ByteDance, Moonshot AI, and StepFun to reject US capital without state approval, responding to Meta's acquisition of Chinese AI startup Manus.
key_facts.excerpt: China plans to restrict its leading technology companies, including top AI startups, from accepting US capital without first obtaining government approval... The move was reportedly in response to Meta's controversial acquisition of startup Manus.

key_facts.fact: The House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced bipartisan export control bills on April 22 that would close loopholes allowing China to access US AI technology, including considering listing distillation entities on the Entity List.
key_facts.excerpt: The House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced a slate of bipartisan export control bills Wednesday that show a growing appetite in Congress for restricting the flow of artificial intelligence technology to China.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has previously accused DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax of conducting distillation attacks against Claude; OpenAI has made similar accusations against DeepSeek for using GPT outputs to train its models.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this year, Anthropic described distillation 'attacks' by three AI laboratories, DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax, saying it had found them all to be working to copy Anthropic models through distillation campaigns.

key_facts.fact: The dual escalation came weeks before a planned Trump visit to Beijing, with China's embassy responding that its AI development 'is the result of its own dedication and effort as well as international cooperation.'
key_facts.excerpt: A representative of China's US embassy in Washington DC said its development was 'the result of its own dedication and effort as well as international cooperation'.

stories.headline: DOJ Arrests US Soldier for $400K+ Polymarket Insider Bet on Maduro Capture He Helped Plan

key_facts.fact: Gannon Ken Van Dyke, a 38-year-old Army special forces soldier at Fort Bragg, was charged with wire fraud, commodities fraud, and theft of nonpublic government information — the first criminal case in the US tied to prediction market wagers.
key_facts.excerpt: The Justice Department and CFTC unsealed an indictment charging Van Dyke with wire fraud, commodities fraud, theft of nonpublic government information — marking the first criminal case in the U.S. tied to prediction market wagers.

key_facts.fact: Van Dyke participated in the planning and execution of the January 2026 predawn raid that captured Maduro, then bet approximately $33,034 across 13 wagers on Polymarket that Maduro would be removed from power, earning over $409,000 in profits.
key_facts.excerpt: The soldier, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, 'participated in the planning and execution of the' operation to capture Maduro, the DOJ said.

key_facts.fact: The CFTC separately filed a civil complaint seeking restitution, disgorgement, trading bans, and a permanent injunction against further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act.
key_facts.excerpt: The CFTC is also pursuing civil penalties, seeking restitution, disgorgement, trading bans, and a permanent injunction against further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act.

key_facts.fact: Van Dyke faces up to 20 years in prison if convicted of the top count (wire fraud) and up to 10 years on each remaining count.
key_facts.excerpt: He faces a maximum possible sentence of 20 years in prison if convicted of the top criminal count, wire fraud, and up to 10 years in each of the remaining counts.

key_facts.fact: Trump, when asked about the arrest, said: 'The whole world, unfortunately, has become somewhat of a casino.' Trump's son Donald Jr. is both an investor in Polymarket and a paid adviser to rival Kalshi.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump, when asked about Van Dyke's arrest and other cases of suspected insider trading on prediction markets, said, 'You know the whole world, unfortunately, has become somewhat of a casino.'
